How to bet on horse racing: Most popular types of wagers     There are a number of different wagering options available on each race, and here we will go through the three traditional bets – Win, Place and Show – as well as the combinations of each. Below are horse racing betting tips that help clarify bet types and the differences between the odds found at sportsbook and racing odds.Each horse will have different odds for each bet type. These odds let you know the horse's expected return on each individual bet type. It's important to note that the odds on each horse fluctuate constantly and payouts are calculated based on the final odds, not the exact odds from the time you place your bet, a major difference from betting on other sports. That is because racetracks use parimutuel wagering.                      Differences in horse racing odds vs. sportsbook odds           Horse racing odds rely on pari-mutuel wagering, which is a system that pools together all of the money bet on each market up until the race begins. The track and the books take a certain percentage or rake for their operations (the Takeout), and the remainder of the pool is then divided among the winning ticket holders. The takeout is divided between the house (track) and horsemen, including race purses.             What is particularly unique about this system for those who are accustomed to betting on sports is that your odds can shift after you place the bet until they lock when the race begins. On sports betting apps, if you bet something at 10-1 and it later moves to 8-1, you still receive the 10-1 payout. In horse racing, your payout will change based on the way the market moves to create the final odds. The final odds you'll be paid out at are determined by how much is bet on each horse and the Takeout.            The standard horse racing unit for win, place, or show bets is $2.                     Win           The win bet is simply betting on which horse will come in first place. Using the 2026 Herbie Dyke Stakes as an example, the winner was Legarto and finished with 12-5 odds. A $2 Win bet paid $6.80, a product of the standard $4.80 for a 12-5 payout on a $2 bet, plus your original $2 wager amount back.                      Place           The Place bet allows you to wager on whether a horse will finish first or second in a race, meaning two Place bets will pay out on each race. This gives you a greater chance of winning, but lowers your odds on the horse if they place.            Using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as the example again, a $2 Place bet on the No. 18 horse only returned $7.50 compared to the $17.96 for a Win bet. But also, a $2 Place bet on the No. 8 horse (Journalism), who was the favorite but came in second, paid $4.94 while the Win bet lost.                       Show           A Show bet is an even more conservative betting option. You are wagering on whether a horse will finish in the top three positions. That means three Show bets will pay out each race. For example, a $2 Show bet on a 10-1 winner returned $4. As one might expect, show bet odds are far less favorable than win bet odds, making them one of the more conservative wagers available in horse racing.                       Win/Place           You can also combine these bets on each horse when you're placing your wagers. That means if you want to bet on a horse to win and place, you can do that. A $2 Win/Place bet really means you're betting $4 – a $2 Win bet and a $2 Place bet. If the horse you bet on wins, you will win both bets. If the horse finishes second, you would only win the Place bet.                       Place/Show           The same is available for a Place/Show bet, where a $2 Place/Show bet would be $4 wagered on a $2 Place bet and a $2 Show bet. If your horse finishes first or second, you would win both, but if it finishes third, you would only win the Show bet.                       Win/Place/Show (Across The Board)            Lastly, you can bet on all three options in what is often referred to as an Across The Board bet. A $2 Across The Board bet would really be $6 wagered – $2 on Win, $2 on Place, and $2 on Show. If you make an Across The Board bet and your horse wins, you pay out on all three wagers.            It's important to note that betting on Win/Place/Show combinations may not result in a net return even if one of the bets pays. For example, at the 2024 Kentucky Derby, an Across The Board bet on the 11 horse would've returned just $5.58 on $6 wagered.                       The most popular horse racing bet types           Many horse racing bettors place exotic bets to try to predict where multiple horses will finish in a race. These combination wagers offer the chance for bigger payouts, but come with a lower probability of winning (just like same game parlays in sports betting).            It is important to note that, unlike sports betting, there is no standard odds calculation to use for determining exotic payouts. Because of parimutuel wagering, odds can fluctuate until the race begins based on which horses are taking the most action. Additionally, live horse racing betting is available to those interested, adding another layer of entertainment for those watching races as they take place.           Exactas           An exacta bet in horse racing functions the same as it does in other sports. The bettor must pick the exact finishing order. For example, if someone wants to place an exacta bet with two horses, they must select each horse and where it will finish exactly. Once again using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as an example, a $2 exacta on the No. 18 and No. 8 horses (who closed with final odds of 7-1 and almost 3-1) paid $48.32. This style of betting can be seen in plenty of other sports, especially in futures betting.Exotics winnings will vary based on the number of horses in the race, the odds of the top-finishing horses, and the size of the pool. For example, the field for the 2024 Kentucky Derby saw a longer shot horse win, so the exacta pool paid $258.56 -- significantly more than the 2025 Derby.                       Trifectas           This horse racing wager is placing a bet on the exact order of the top-three finishers in a race. A straight trifecta will pay handsomely, but is extremely difficult to hit. Trifecta payouts are often shown for $0.50 bets, but some will show for $1 bets as well. The payout screen will tell you which, but that's important to note so you're aware of how much you are getting back.            The 2025 Kentucky Derby Trifecta paid $231.12 on a $1 Trifecta bet.                       Superfectas           Superfecta bets try to predict the exact order of the top-four finishers in a horse race. The superfecta payout is usually shown for a $1 bet. For the 2025 Kentucky Derby, a $1 superfecta that added the fourth-place No. 3 horse to the trifecta paid $1,682.27.                      Super High 5           Some books will even allow you to bet on the top-five finishers in their exact order in what is called a Super High 5 bet. Those payouts will again be shown for a $1 wager. The odds of hitting a Super High 5, especially in a large field race, are exceptionally low. They are equivalent to multi-leg futures parlays in sports betting.The 2025 Kentucky Derby's $1 Super High Five paid $38,405.96.                      Box           A box bet allows you to have every possible combination for exotics. If you think you know which two horses will hit the exacta but are not sure of their specific order, you can box it. The same goes for trifectas and superfectas. The more horses you box together, the lower your total profits on the payout will be.            For example, a three-horse exacta box bet costs $12 to bet, as you are betting $2 on all six potential combinations between those three horses:           $2 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 3 second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 1 in first and No. 3 in secondYou can do the same for Trifectas and Superfectas, but at exponentially escalating costs. A $1 Trifecta Box with three horses is six combinations, so $6 wagered:           $1 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 1 in first, No. 3 in second, No. 2 in first$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 2 in third$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 1 in firstFrom there, four horses in a $1 trifecta box is 24 combinations for $24 wagered. Five horses is 60 possible combinations for $60.            A $1 Superfecta box of four horses is $24 wagered, five horses is $120 wagered and six horses is $360 wagered.                       How to bet on horse racing: Multi-race wagers           While those exotics offer a variety of options for betting on individual races, you can also bet on multiple races at the same track in various ways. These combination wagers pay out based on the betting pool, allowing you to choose a handful of horses you're confident in throughout the day to increase your potential payout.                       Daily Double           The Daily Double is exactly what it sounds like: Betting on back-to-back race winners from that day. The odds for Daily Doubles vary based on the odds for the individual horses you bet and the overall Daily Double betting pool. As an example, the $2 Daily Double at Horseshoe Indianapolis on April 15, 2025 from the first two races with the 7 horse in the first race (went off at 1-1 odds) and the 4 horse in the second race (went off at 3-5 odds) paid $8.            Once the first race ends, the payouts for each potential Daily Double will be shown under a "Will Pays" tab on the next race's betting screen.                       Pick-3, Pick-4, Pick-5 and Pick-6           Along with the Daily Double, there are more options for betting the winner of multiple races in a row at the same track. The Pick-3 is picking the winner in three consecutive races, the Pick-4 in four consecutive races, and so on for the Pick-5 and Pick-6.           Like exotics, the pool amount and the odds for each horse wagered on determine the payouts for these multi-race wagers. The default unit for these bets varies from book to book, with FanDuel showing $0.50 payouts and TwinSpires showing $1 payouts in the Will Pays section.            The more races you put together on a ticket, the more you can win. But as with any multi-race wager, the more legs you add, the harder it is to win. In this way, these bets function similarly to parlays in other sports.For some of the biggest races, the Pick-6 will feature a set guaranteed prize pool for the winner(s) no matter what the actual wagered amount is. The 2024 Kentucky Derby featured a $1 million guaranteed pool on TwinSpires for Pick-6s on races 6 through 11 at Churchill Downs.                       Understanding horse racing payouts           After the race, the winning payouts will be displayed for each bet type. The standard unit for win/place/show and exactas is a $2 bet. Trifectas, superfectas and super high 5s are typically shown as $1 or $0.50, but will say explicitly which on the payout board.            The payouts for each horse in the top three for the 2025 Kentucky Derby looked as follows:           2025 Kentucky DerbyWinPlaceShowSovereignty (No. 18) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$17.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$7.50 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$5.58 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Journalism (No. 8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								           $4.94 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$3.70 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Baeza (No. 21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								           				           $8.38 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				           If you bet more (or less) than the standard $2 unit, you multiply the payout by how much you bet and divide by the standard unit. For example, a $10 Win bet on Sovereignty returned $89.80, while a $25 Show bet on Journalism would've returned $46.25.            For the single-race exotics at the 2025 Kentucky Derby, the payouts were as follows:            2025 Kentucky DerbyPayout$2 Exacta (18-8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$48.32 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Trifecta (18-8-21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$231.12 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Superfecta (18-8-21-3) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1,682.27 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Super High 5 (18-8-21-3-20) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$38,405.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				          Biggest horse races beyond Kentucky Derby betting          The horse racing calendar operates year-round, but there are six events on the schedule that serve as the most important, thus attracting the best fields. The three Triple Crown events headline for the general public, but the Breeders' Cup, Pegasus World Cup and Dubai World Cup all offer massive purses and attract some of the best horses and fields in all of racing.           October 30-31, 2026: Breeders' Cup January 23, 2027: Pegasus World CupMarch 27, 2027: Dubai World CupMay 1, 2027: Kentucky DerbyMay 15, 2027: Preakness StakesJune 5, 2027: Belmont Stakes           Triple Crown of horse racing           The Kentucky Derby, Preakness Stakes and Belmont Stakes make up horse racing's Triple Crown. There are 13 horses that have completed the Triple Crown, winning all three events, and just two – American Pharoah (2015) and Justify (2018) – have accomplished that feat in the 21st century.            Not every horse competes in all three Triple Crown events. Each race operates at different lengths, and the turnaround time can be too quick for trainers to be comfortable running their horse in one after the other. Some Derby winners don't run the Preakness, while some have made it two legs before withdrawing from the Belmont.            The Kentucky Derby is a 1 1/4 mile race, the Preakness Stakes is 1 3/16 mile, and the Belmont Stakes is a grueling 1 1/2 mile event (although it is being run currently at 1 1/4 mile at Saratoga Race Course due to renovations at Belmont Park).                       Tips and advice for betting on horse racing           There are a number of strategies for betting on horse racing, but it all starts with understanding the horses and knowing their strengths, weaknesses and past performances.                       Racing forms and past performances           These are race-day publications and programs available at tracks and online to preview the day's races at each track. They are full of data and information from past races. All of the best horse racing betting apps have integrated much of this information into their betting screen.                       Track conditions           Before you even get to the horses, understanding track conditions is vital. Knowing if a track is dirt or grass, firm and fast or soft and slow, is critical information to know so you can look at which horses in a given race run best in certain conditions.                       Horse tendencies            From there, you want to understand the tendencies of horses in the field. Some horses get out to fast starts and try to push the pace, while others hang back and try to make a late kick. If most of the field is expected to push the pace and run it fast, then a horse that prefers to stay back may be at an advantage due to an unsustainable early pace.            The opposite could be true, too; if the pace is going to be slower early, frontrunners are more likely to hold their position. Some of this information can be found in PPs or Past Performance data.                       Post position           Post position can also matter to a horse's success. Some prefer to run the rail (on the inside of the track) while others prefer being on the outside and having more space. This information is all worth considering and comparing with the other horses in the field.                      Trainer and jockey information           A horse's trainer and jockey will also have tendencies. Some trainers are better at getting horses ready for a certain type of track, but maybe don't have a great track record at others. Some jockeys may be more or less aggressive on the track, which may or may not work well with that specific horse's tendencies, or they may have a long track record with that horse and know how to get the most out of them.                       Workout times           There's also plenty of data available that can help you. Workout times, if available, can give you an idea of how a horse has been running in training before a big race.                       Speed figures           Speed figures are like advanced stats of the horse racing world, offering a metric to show how well a horse has been running in its recent races that factors in things like field strength and track quality.            Taking all of that data into account is important to betting on horse racing, and for beginners it's best to ease in and do as much observing as you do betting. You'll start to find certain trends for horses, jockeys, trainers and tracks that can help you find edges on the odds board going forward.                      Manage your horse racing betting bankroll           Managing your bankroll with what percentage of money you have set aside for horse racing betting is vital to increasing your chances of scoring big at some point. Just like in sports betting, where most bankroll management experts advise no more than 2% of your bankroll should be bet on any given game, the same principle can be applied to any given horse race.                       Rules and responsible gaming           Responsible gambling is taken very seriously across all racebooks. All provide the necessary resources and contact information if you or someone you know may have a gambling problem. The minimum age is 18 for horse racing betting in most states, but it is 21 in some states.           Responsible gambling resources include the National Council for Problem Gambling (NCPG) and Gamblers Anonymous. Be smart. Bet smart. Wager responsibly. Those in need of help can also call or text 1-800-GAMBLER (1-800-426-2537). Help is available 24 hours a day and seven days a week.           FAQHow to bet on horse racing?There are several ways to bet on horse racing. The most common methods are through horse racing betting apps like TwinSpires, FanDuel Racing, and DraftKings Horse. Users can bet on a variety of outcomes, with the most common wager coming on which horse will win the given race outright.How to bet on horse racing online?Online horse racing betting is widely accessible. TwinSpires, DraftKings Horse, and FanDuel Racing all provide users with a huge array of betting options on all major races.What is a box bet in horse racing?A box bet in horse racing involves picking the finishing order of the horses. Wagerers can choose the order of the first two, three, four, or five finishers, with the return on their bet increasing with every additional horse they include in their wager. If a bettor chooses three horses for a box bet, they do not need to finish in an exact order. If they make up the top three, the bet is successful.What is a show bet in horse racing?A show bet is a wager on a specific horse to finish among the top three horses in a given race. Show bets are extremely common wagers that offer less risk and smaller payouts.What is a key box bet in horse racing?A key box bet, unsurprisingly, functions similarly to a box bet. A bettor can select a "key" horse that they believe will finish in an exact position while rounding out the rest of the box in the same fashion as a regular box bet. For example, a bettor could select Horse A to finish first while picking Horses C, B, and D to round out the top four. However, if Horse A does not finish first, the bet loses.

body:
I have exciting news! My rankings will be on CBS! I'll let you know when they are. Another exciting piece of news for the FFT NL crew -- I have finalized in-season planning for Beyond the Box Score, and my intention is to bring you a massive SEVEN weekly Beyond The Boxscore shows. I can confirm that Dan the man and I will be recording multiple times per week! I also intend to produce weekly solo shows where I provide an in-depth usage breakdown for every position to keep you in the know regarding all of your sicko needs.I also can confirm that Ryan Heath will be joining BTB on a weekly basis once again! We're tackling a new project together this year, so be on the lookout for that! And more good news, I'm teaming up with Theo Gremminger twice each week to provide y'all with top notch content! The OG will join BTB early in the week to reflect on the previous week's outcomes, and I'll join Rotowire late in the week to speculate on the upcoming week's outcomes.The original BTB crew (Adam Aizer, Dan, and I) will bring you advanced data on Mondays, as per usual -- be sure to be on the lookout for Aizer's tweets leading up to that show, if you send in good questions, we will talk about them on Monday!BTB will be live on Tuesdays and Thursdays, in addition to the Monday morning live show with Adam on the main FFT channel! You will also find me live on Sunday mornings as a reoccurring guest for the FFT start/sit show!
It's a busy time of year, but it's also my favorite time of year! Football is here! Dan Schneier and I will present our FINAL rankings for each position next week on BTB! Let's lock in and win some leagues!
                                                                    Imagn Images                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
                                                            What defines a league-winner?Nobody knows what it means. It's provocative. It gets the people going!If you want an attempt at quantifying it, maybe you'll enjoy this conversation with Ryan Heath of Fantasy Points Data.Jonathon Brooks, RB, Carolina PanthersI could be overstating his importance (Carolina's offensive line injuries concern me), but Jonathon Brooks feels like the cheapest potential bell-cow RB who might actually be an awesome talent available in 2026 drafts. Bell-cow running backs are extremely important for Fantasy! If we can land on outside of the first few rounds, it's a massive influx of upside for our Fantasy squads.
Depending on how Chuba Hubbard's hamstring cooperates, there's a chance that Brooks sees a large workload early and never lets go of it. Brooks was the first player I discussed in the 'Welcome Back' show on Beyond the Box Score, because I believe he might be a defining aspect of the 2026 draft season. I don't see any other potential three-down skill-sets available anywhere near Brooks, even as his ADP rises. There are a few names who could profile similarly -- Jaylen Warren, Rhamondre Stevenson, and Rashaad White -- but it would require a backfield teammate to falter or miss time with an injury. Brooks is sharing a backfield with an already-injured player who we saw underperform while struggling with health last year -- Hubbard already has seen this coaching staff give his lead back duties to another RB.Round 1-2 turn could produce multiple RB league-winnersThis range of Fantasy Football drafts produces league winners at a really high rate (relatively speaking). And in 2026, this range of drafts is dominated by the RB position. What is one to do when on the clock and staring at a list of awesome running backs?! Earlier this week on CBSSports.com, I profiled each back for Fantasy purposes -- offering my perception of their ceiling, floor, and stability. Here's my breakdown of the league-winning Rounds 1-2 running backs.A.J. Brown, WR, New England Patriots
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            Here's my AJB case. I view him as one of the most-likely candidates to finish WR1 overall.
The podcast that I linked in reference to AJB is great, there are tons of nuggets in there. This link should take you to a discussion about the Chicago Bears.I do not think that there are too many mouths to feed in Chicago. Even if Caleb Williams does not take a step forward (by the way, I feel cautiously optimistic that a step forward is coming -- Ben Johnson's tone has completely shifted over the past 365 days), the WR production we saw from Chicago last year was strong enough to facilitate a strong performance from at least the team's WR1.Luther Burden, WR, Chicago BearsIf he beats out Rome Odunze for targets (here's why I think that he will), Luther Burden can absolutely produce with even just the same offensive environment provided by the first year of Johnson's tenure in Chicago. I expect more from this offense in Year 2 under Johnson. And I expect Burden to play a huge role within the offense.
Tucker Kraft, TE, Green Bay PackersThe Packers have so much target vacancy to be accounted for. Christian Watson's career-high targets in a game is 10, and he's only been above eight twice. Jayden Reed's career-high targets in a game is also 10, and that's the only time he's had more than eight targets in a game. Those two have been extremely efficient per-target players, but neither has been targeted at a high rate.Matthew Golden had just a 15.7% target share at the University of Texas in 2024. His target share was above 20% in only 3 of 16 games.Is Tucker Kraft (target totals of 9 and 10 in two games before his ACL injury last year) going to suddenly play a larger-than-seen-before role? That seemed to be the way things were trending in 2025. It's worth remembering that Jayden Reed was out in both of those games and Christian Watson missed the first and played a partial role in his return from ACL surgery in the second "big Kraft target game."
Jordan Love and Matt LaFleur talk about Kraft like he's "Jordan's guy."Kraft was definitely the player trusted when in scoring distance. I wonder how realistic it is to expect the target shares we were seeing before his injury sustain over a larger sample size. If we get anything similar to that, Kraft -- a player who has been unbelievably efficient on a per-target basis -- could burn Fantasy leagues to the ground if healthy. The best outcome for Kraft is that he's a rare every-down tight end who can push his route rate into the 90% range, create yards after the catch (at a league-best rate), and convert red zone targets into scores.What if he's not ready for all that, yet, though?It would mark a pretty significant leap in his progression for Kraft -- even if not recovering from a reconstructed knee 00 to suddenly operate like a primary target, though. This is why I'm so high on Reed and Watson as 2026 discounts. History tells us that Watson and Reed are more likely to step into that type of a role. Most pass games use outside receivers as the primary read, so Watson in particular looks promising.Last year, Green Bay had seven instances of a pass-catcher reaching a first-read target share of 33% or higher -- Kraft did it once, Dontayvion Wicks did it once, Romeo Doubs did it twice, and Watson hit that rate three times (consecutive rates of 33%, 40%, and 35% across Weeks 11-13).
Watson returned in Week 8 but was not a full-time player until Week 10. From Week 11 on, he had a first-read target rate of 29.4%, and his rate never dipped below 20%. I wondered if his massively-high average depth of target came down during that stretch, but it was still 15.8 yards. That's so high!It's very rare to be productive for Fantasy with such a high aDOT. Even the best players who fall in that range (Alec Pierce and Jameson Williams last year) aren't able to push target shares much higher than 23-25%. This again leads me to Reed as a potential league-winner in 2026. Maybe it's Golden. The case feels so clear with Reed, though.Kraft has the talent to win people leagues. If he's not ready to fill that type of a role, then that means even more volume could shift over to the receivers. And the receivers already are expected to pick up the slack in replacing Wicks and Doubs. I know that betting on Packers receivers has been frustrating in the past, but it really feels like this is a clear source of potential league-winning value depending on how the target distribution shakes out.
Oronde Gadsden II, TE, Los Angeles Chargers I thought long and hard about who I wanted to write about among the Chargers pass-catchers. My belief is that Ladd McConkey is the most-likely player to put together a huge season. His price tag suggests as much. I still think there's plenty of room for McConkey to be a great pick at ADP, but Quentin Johnston and Year 2 tight end Oronde Gadsden II were the two who I kept feeling compelled to write about.I landed on Gadsden for reasons similar to Kraft. If he hits, Gadsden profiles as a meaningful red zone weapon who might also add some yardage juice with his unique skill set as a receiver. If Gadsden plays a meaningful role, not only will he be a hit (Year 2 tight ends often do!) as a late-round TE, but it also could detract from the ceiling cases for McConkey and QJ. Conversely, what if Gadsden ends up phased out? David Njoku and Charlie Kolar present more of a 50/50 proposition to opposing defenses. If one or both of those two are in the game, it's not clear if the Chargers will run or pass. If Gadsden is in, it's likely a pass. The Chargers also have a fullback who Mike McDaniel is a known fan of. It's possible that Gadsden simply won't matter much for an offense focused on establishing an effective run game.That's why I settled on him as a player who might 'define' 2026 Fantasy Football. How do you feel about Gadsden? If you don't expect him to be prioritized, then you probably should be drafting a lot of McConkey or QJ or both. (Also, shoutout BTB favorite Tre Harris, always)
Jaxson Dart, QB, New York GiantsJaxson Dart is one of five QBs to average 20+ Fantasy points per game (only including starts) as a rookie, dating back to 2000. He was one of, if not outright the best, playmaker at the QB position last year.Still, Dart is relatively cheap in 2026 drafts. We do not know what to expect from this coaching staff, but I have not heard a single analyst all summer with even a little bit of cope that the coaching might not be that bad. Universally the Fantasy community feels terrified of this situation.It feels like so much will fall on Dart's shoulders to simply be good enough to make things work in this offense. And, he kind of did last year, without Malik Nabers! If Dart is simply really good, this offense could produce some massive Fantasy producers. The schedule looks really favorable in the second-half of the season. Players like Nabers and Cam Skattebo could produce huge results at decent discounts in drafts. Do you feel like betting on this situation?
The Minnesota VikingsI can't get over how favorable Minnesota's schedule is. Ever since digging into it with Dan, Minnesota's schedule has remained ingrained in my brain as a potentially important part of 2026 Fantasy Football. This offense was so incredibly disappointing in 2025. It's tough for drafters to wash such a nasty taste from their mouths. If the offense rebounds in 2026, this schedule could facilitate incredible Fantasy outcomes for some severely discounted players.The toughest defenses I see -- on paper -- on Minnesota's schedule are the Packers and 49ers. And one of those matchups vs. Green Bay comes in Week 1 without Micah Parsons. Beyond that, the toughest matchups might be Saints, Panthers, and Bills. It's an incredible soft schedule, and on top of the advantageous defensive matchups, the Vikings also could benefit from facing some good offenses. We could see some shootouts if the Vikings offense can put points on the board.I'm coming around on this backfield as a potentially really value source in 2026. A return to health for the tackles could provide a big boost, and I'm intrigued to see what Frank Smith (formerly worked with Mike McDaniel in Miami) might do in revamping Minnesota's scheme. Demond Claiborne is one of my favorite late-round stashes, and I see either Jordan Mason or Aaron Jones as viable picks in drafts where they fall. You might get early-season production, and with good luck, potentially a full season of value.The passing game is the crux of the Minnesota outcome. And, of course, we have no idea what to expect. I see some concerning signs for Justin Jefferson, in terms of the pairing with Kyler Murray. He's the one who I have the hardest time ever clicking in drafts. Everyone else in this offense feels like a value. But if we see Minnesota put points on the board, Jefferson will probably be a huge part of it. His target shares have never been higher than the last two seasons. We just need the overall passing production in Minnesota to be better for it to matter.The Tampa Bay BuccaneersNobody knows what to expect from Bucky Irving. Nobody really even knows what to expect from Emeka Egbuka, especially now that a toe injury is part of the equation. I am really excited about how Zac Robinson can affect change in Tampa. Pair that with a return to health for a potentially mauling offensive line, and this Bucs offense is one that I want to aggressively attack in drafts.If you don't believe in Bucky, you absolutely should be scooping up a ton of Kenneth Gainwell at his ADP. I believe in Bucky. The most interesting value on this offense might actually be Chris Godwin. Camp reports are good -- Godwin is expected to play an important role once again, and as my buddy Ryan Heath astutely pointed out, Godwin has been extremely efficient when used in motion at the snap of the football. Robinson has used motion at snap at the highest rate of any play-caller over the past two years.I even think that we could get surprise Fantasy viability from an ancillary piece such as Cade Otton or Jalen McMillan if Baker blows the league up on his "pay me" tour. And what if the Egbuka injury lingers? This team has a plethora of talented receivers. If there's an injury to any of the top guys, we could see Tez Johnson benefit in a huge way from free releases at the line of scrimmage within Robinson's design. Rookie Ted Hurst has some serious juice.There's a ton to like in Tampa's offense, and we truly have no idea how the volume is going to be distributed. I want to lean into that uncertainty and pile up as many Bucs as I can on my Fantasy squads. And, of course, I love landing Baker as a late-round QB.Good luck to anybody drafting this weekend! Keep an eye on your inbox! Rankings updates will be coming your way soon!

Castellanos is looking to bring his dual-threat ability back to the college ranks after being granted a fifth year of eligibility

        After receiving a fifth year of eligibility, former Florida State quarterback Thomas Castellanos has entered the NCAA transfer portal, sources tell CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz.On Friday, a Kentucky judge granted a temporary injunction in an eligibility lawsuit that included Castellanos and former Missouri basketball standout Mark Mitchell. Because Castellanos now has an injunction, he will not be affected by the new ruling in the Colorado lawsuit that took away eligibility for qualified athletes in the class of 2022.A three-star recruit out of Georgia, Castellanos signed with UCF as a member of the 2022 recruiting class. The following season, Castellanos transferred to Boston College, where he started across two seasons before jumping to Florida State as a senior in 2025.Last year, Castellanos completed 58.3% of his passes for 2,760 yards, 15 touchdowns and nine interceptions while also rushing for 557 yards and nine touchdowns. While Castellanos' lone season with the Seminoles was turbulent, he led the team to an upset of No. 8 Alabama in Week 1.Throughout his college career, Castellanos has provided dynamic playmaking with his legs, and he even rushed for 1,113 yards as a sophomore at Boston College. Despite missing spring practice and most of fall camp, Castellanos has already reportedly generated significant interest from at least one Power Four team.
Where will Castellanos land?Texas Tech has emerged as the most likely landing spot for Castellanos as he looks to continue his college career, according to multiple reports. Given how the quarterback situation has evolved in Lubbock throughout the offseason, landing with the Red Raiders makes plenty of sense for Castellanos.Texas Tech paid up to land Cincinnati transfer Brendan Sorsby out of the transfer portal, but due to fallout from a gambling scandal, Sorsby will no longer play for the Red Raiders this fall. Will Hammond — very talented in his own right — is now the starter, but he's coming off a torn ACL he suffered last October.While the Red Raiders are still fine at the top of the quarterback depth chart, the loss of Sorsby made them much shallower. Sophomore Lloyd Jones III is currently set to back up Hammond, but he's attempted just five passes at the college level. Castellanos would give Texas Tech more insurance at the most important position on the field.
That's important because the rest of the Texas Tech roster looks to be a legitimate College Football Playoff threat. The Red Raiders brought in 22 players via the portal, and that class ranked No. 6 nationally, according to 247Sports. Castellanos would help ensure that those title hopes won't be immediately derailed if Hammond is unable to play.

Serie A is finally back! The 2026-2027 Serie A season will kick off this weekend in Italy, with Inter, the 2025-2026 Scudetto winners, looking to defend the title in the new season. AC Milan, their cross-city rivals, made some key signings in the summer after replacing the coach and the whole club hierarchy after the disappointing end of the last campaign, and appointed former Manchester United coach Ruben Amorim to lead the new cycle. Six teams replaced their coaches, including Napoli, which saw Antonio Conte leave the Azzurri after two seasons and appointed former AC Milan and Juventus manager Massimiliano Allegri. Let's take a look at our power rankings ahead of the upcoming season: 1. Inter The 2025-2026 Serie A champions are still the favorites to replicate the success of the past season. They lost a key player in Denzel Dumfries, who joined Real Madrid, but replaced him with Djed Spence and signed other players like John Stones and Curtis Jones who can help Cristian Chivu win another Scudetto. Overall, they have a stronger squad compared to the one that won the most recent Serie A title. 2. AC Milan The Rossoneri spent big money in the summer to support American Christian Pulisic and signed striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG who became the highest paid player in the history of the club, after Gerry Cardinale's side spent over $70 million to sign the Portuguese striker. On top of him, they also signed Mario Gila from Lazio for around $20 million and Diego Moreira from Strasbourg for more than $60 million. However, the biggest decision was to appoint Ruben Amorim to replace Massimiliano Allegri, who failed to bring the Rossoneri back to Champions League soccer. 3. NapoliIt didn't take long time for Allegri to find a new club as Napoli decided to hire him after Antonio Conte's decision to leave the Azzurri ahead of the summer. Allegri, who has signed a three-year deal with the Italian club, will be expected to improve Napoli's performances, particularly in the Champions League, as demanded by club owner Aurelio De Laurentiis. Napoli have a strong squad, but last season their campaign was severely affected by injuries.
4. AS Roma  The side coached by Gian Piero Gasperini clinched a Champions League spot at the end of a successful campaign, but it will now be much more complicated to replicate the same success. They have a chance to make a deep run, and the roster is also strong enough to achieve the targets requested by the fan base and the ownership. Winning a trophy, maybe the Coppa Italia, could be a major milestone for the new project, now entering its second year, led by the former Atalanta manager. 5. Como Como were one of the biggest surprises of the 2025–26 season but maybe not entirely unexpectedly. Their fourth-place finish and historic qualification for the Champions League were remarkable, but the team led by Cesc Fabregas wants more. They re-signed Nico Paz from Real Madrid for $60 million, arguably the most important Serie A signing of the summer. The only doubt about them is how they will deal with the two major competitions at the same time, but watch out for them, once again. 6. JuventusDespite confirming head coach Luciano Spalletti for at least another season, everything has changed again at the club with a new CEO in Giovanni Carnevali, an experienced Italian director who can lead the new cycle. Some of the signings were interesting, such as the one of Kerim Alajbegovic from Bayer Leverkusen or the one of Randal Kolo Muani from PSG. Others, like the one of Guglielmo Vicario on loan from Tottenham as the new starting goalkeeper, are not what we expected. 
7. FiorentinaI strongly believe they will be the surprise of the season, after risking relegation last year. Former Tottenham and Juventus director Fabio Paratici is leading the sporting project and has signed multiple talents, starting with Franco Mastantuono on loan from Real Madrid, and appointed a young talented coach like Fabio Grosso, who previously coached Sassuolo in the Italian first division. Fiorentina might finally be back. 8. AtalantaNothing against the club and the job they've done over the past years, but when you sign a coach like Maurizio Sarri you can expect your team to perform more on the long term, missing out some key points in the first part of the season. This is why I think they can aim for European soccer, but it won't be that easy. 9. GenoaAnother team I think will do well. Under Daniele De Rossi's management, Genoa were a surprising side in the second part of the season, and in his full campaign in charge I think there's a big chance to see them as one of the surprises of the Serie A season. 
10. BolognaIt will be difficult for them after Vincenzo Italiano decided to leave the Italian side to join Besiktas. They hired a coach like Domenico Tedesco, who will make his Serie A debut this weekend: A risky choice. 11. UdineseOne of those teams that always seem to find themselves in the same position at the start of the season: unlikely to face a relegation battle, but equally unlikely to challenge for a European spot.12. Torino I'm curious to see the impact of Ignazio Abate in Serie A after bringing Juve Stabia, a team that was placed under judicial administration as prosecutors stated the Serie B club was used as a tool by the local Camorra mafia clan, to the playoffs last season; now he has his first big chance in the Italian top flight. 
13. SassuoloGiovanni Carnevali, the former club CEO and the mastermind behind the success of the Neroverdi in the past years, has left his position and joined Juventus this summer. While Fabio Grosso left the club to take over at Fiorentina and most of the key players stayed, the club appointed Alberto Aquilani as his successor. Aquilani, who led Catanzaro to the Serie B playoff final in June, is widely regarded as one of the most talented young managers in Italy.14. ParmaThe Crociati survived the Italian first division under Carlos Cuesta last season, the youngest coach in the league and aim to do the same this year despite selling some key players, such as Zion Suzuki and Gabriel Strefezza. 15. CagliariThe first season under Vincenzo Pisacane was a success overall as the team managed to avoid relegation, and this season we can expect more from them, but it won't be easier. 
16. LazioThere are not many hopes around Lazio this season after hiring Gennaro Gattuso as the new head coach. The Biancocelesti had another disappointing summer transfer window, as they saw some key players leaving such as Mario Gila who joined AC Milan and had to face a net-zero transfer window for the summer 2026 session. In this worrying financial environment, a tumble down the table is a real possibility17. VeneziaTheir plans for a new stadium are already underway, but if you get the chance to go and watch a match at the current Penzo Stadium, do it. It's an unforgettable experience.18. MonzaThe club made some signings in the summer, but none of them are capable of keeping the team in the first division. Am I too drastic? Probably not. 
19. LecceEusebio Di Francesco finally managed to keep Lecce in the top flight after suffering relegation twice in two years with Frosinone and Venezia. However, I think keeping them up this time will be an even bigger challenge.20. FrosinoneThis is what Massimiliano Alvini, the head coach, said about the transfer window. "I wasn't involved. As the coach, you have to understand the characteristics of the new signings. It will take time, months, to fully integrate them." I don't see them avoiding relegation, do you?
